subject: Clarify: regional model binding + fallback constraints for BrightHealth
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brighthealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model locality & fallback question for PROD launch

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Security flagged two items we need clarified before production sign-off for BrightHealth’s integration: 1) We need the model serving to be strictly bound to our US-only VPC (no routing to other regions), and 2) we cannot allow automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant that might run outside our control plane (even as a transient fallback).

Attached is an excerpt of our security checklist with the relevant lines highlighted. Can Redwood confirm whether you support a hard regional bind + explicit no-fallback policy? If not, what are the engineering trade-offs and a proposed workaround that meets our compliance needs?

We’re targeting a soft-golive on Aug 2. Appreciate a quick note on feasibility and any timeline impact.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Product Lead, Integrations
BrightHealth

Attachment: BrightHealth_Security_Reqs_v2.pdf

Forwarding BrightHealth’s ask — copy of their security checklist attached. High level: they want a hard US-only binding and explicit prohibition on any fallback to a different variant/region. This is an exception to our default routing/fallback policy. Thoughts on whether we can enforce this without breaking SLOs or the existing routing mesh?

Priority: high — external wants answer this week. If we need an ops/process workaround (e.g., pre-provision dedicated nodes + deny cross-region routing at the router level), flag costs and lead time.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: BrightHealth_Security_Reqs_v2.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model locality & fallback question for PROD launch

FWIW from infra: technically we can implement a strict region lock for a customer by tagging their workload and refusing cross-region routing at the service proxy level. That prevents traffic steering and automatic fallback to other regions. However, two caveats:

- Availability/capacity: If their pinned region loses capacity, the request would fail instead of falling back. We’d need a dedicated capacity reservation (dedicated or reserved slots) to meet their SLA; that adds cost and procurement.
- Model variants: If they also require a strict model binary (quantized variant X only), we can pin model_version and disable automated model substitution, but this increases operational burden for rollouts and removes one of our cost-smoothing levers (auto-fallback to a cpu/cheap-quant variant).

Proposed route: offer a short-term carveout: 1) dedicate a small pool of gpus in us-west-2, 2) enforce region lock at proxy, 3) document an agreed risk that in extreme capacity events we will notify and fail (or we can offer a paid cross-region standby). I’ll estimate costs if you want to propose this to the customer.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brighthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model locality & fallback question for PROD launch

Thanks — quick commercial perspective: BrightHealth is an early enterprise customer with a likely >$150k ARR initial contract. They’ll pay for additional operational guarantees, but we need a clear mutual action plan. If we go the dedicated-reservation route, commercial wants a defined monthly commitment + an escalation playbook for capacity incidents.

Suggested customer-facing options to present (ranked):
1) Dedicated US-only pool (recommended): upfront one-month reserve + monthly minimum; we guarantee no cross-region routing and no automated fallback.
2) US-policy + paid standby fallback: strict US routing with a paid, preapproved cross-region standby that fires only with pre-agreed approvals (keeps some flexibility).
3) Standard hosted with SLO caveats: explain risks (best-effort, falls back per routing policy).

I’ve looped Sarah from BrightHealth to confirm which option they prefer and to surface commercial constraints. If they pick #1 I’ll need an engineering contact to scope the exact capacity profile and initial commit.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brighthealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model locality & fallback question for PROD launch

Sarah — thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Based on infra input and commercial options below, we can support a hard regional lock + no-automatic-fallback with the following binding terms: 

- Implementation: pre-provisioned dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 and policy enforcement at the proxy/router so that no requests are routed outside the customer VPC.
- Model pinning: we will pin a specific model_version and disable automatic variant substitution; any model changes require a scheduled maintenance window and mutual signoff.
- Failover behavior: by default requests will fail if the dedicated pool is fully saturated; optional paid standby cross-region fallback is available with preapproval.
- Commercials & timeline: provisioning + validation ~3 weeks from signed commitment; estimated monthly commit $18k (initial sizing estimate — will update after infra sizing).

Next steps: Vanessa will capture the commercial option you prefer and prepare a short mutual action plan; Priyom will run a sizing exercise and return a firm monthly commit number. If BrightHealth confirms option #1 (dedicated pool), we’ll prepare an exception SOW and an ops runbook describing the no-fallback enforcement and incident escalation.

—Soojin
Sooin Lee (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

summary: BrightHealth requests a strict US-only model serving binding and prohibition on automatic cross-region fallback. Internal discussion weighs technical feasibility, availability risks, and commercial options: dedicated US-only GPU pool (recommended), paid standby fallback, or standard hosted with SLO caveats. Proposed next steps: sizing, commercial MPA, and exception SOW if customer selects dedicated pool.
